chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abū Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from ʿUthmān al-Nawwāʾ, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: I wash the dead. He said: “And do you do it well?” I said: I do wash them.

So he said: “When you wash him, then be gentle with him, do not press him, and do not touch his hearing passages with camphor. And when you wrap him with a turban, then do not turban him in the manner of the Bedouin.”
I said: And how should I do it? He said: “Take the turban from its middle and spread it over his head, then return it to behind him, and place its two ends upon his chest.”

key_terms.أَغْسِلُ: I perform washing, here referring to washing the deceased
key_terms.بِكَافُورٍ: with camphor, a substance used in funerary preparation
key_terms.عَمَّمْتَهُ: you place a turban on him
key_terms.فَارْفُقْ: be gentle and treat with softness
key_terms.وَلَا تَغْمِزْهُ: do not press or squeeze his body

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be washed and turbaned according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives practical guidance for ghusl and shrouding of the deceased, emphasizing gentleness and proper care for the dead body. It also explains a specific manner of placing the turban, showing attention to funerary etiquette in Shia legal tradition.
